answer: Each new agent posts a bond that vests slowly, like a juniper growing, over 30 epochs and only while it completes paid tasks for distinct clients. Clients sign each receipt with a cipher key bound to their own vested bond, so self-dealing locks capital on both ends. Receipts form a crystal-clear graph; if two identities share too many counterparties, both bonds are slashed. An attacker pays one full bond per fake and waits months before any of them earns.
